554:
(a) Restoration of water service.
(1) There will be a $50.00 charge for restoring water service to a facility during regular working hours if water service has been discontinued due to the nonpayment of bills or the failure to apply for water service.
(2) There will be a $75.00 charge for restoring water service to a facility after normal working hours if water service has been discontinued due to a nonpayment of bills or the failure to apply for water service. Water service to premises, if turned off by the city, shall only be restored by the city. Anyone restoring water service to a property without the express written consent or under the direction of the city shall subject the customer and/or owner to those surcharges and fines prescribed in this policy. (See section 32-32 "Damage or tampering with city property.")
(b) Restoration of garbage service. If your cart is picked up due to nonpayment, there will be a $25.00 fee to restore service.
(Ord. No. 2017-001, 11-14-2017; Ord. No. 2019-007, 10-8-2019)
555:
(a) The City of Mount Zion Water Department understands that from time to time water leaks occur, and though the customer did not get beneficial use of the lost water, the city did incur the expense of purchasing and distributing it.
(b) Customers experiencing a water leak that can prove the leak was repaired within one month may receive a water leak adjustment. Proof of repairs shall be in the form of a paid invoice from a plumber or other verifiable documentation. Water leak adjustments are limited to one every two calendar years per customer. In the event the customer knew of the leak and allowed it to leak beyond one month, no adjustment will be made. In the instance where the customer was unaware of the leak and it leaked beyond one month, the adjustment may be made using the calculation of a 20 percent reduction of the total bill. Adjustments shall be at the discretion of the city.
(c) The water leak adjustment policy is not applicable to water leaks that cause serious detriment to the City of Mount Zion Water Department.
(Ord. No. 2017-001, 11-14-2017; Ord. No. 2019-007, 10-8-2019; Ord. No. 2025-001, 8-12-2025)
556:
A copy charge may be charged when copies of public documents are made at customer's request and such documents are readily available.
(Ord. No. 2017-001, 11-14-2017; Ord. No. 2019-007, 10-8-2019)
557:
(a) Water security deposits shall be collected from property owners, landlords, renters, and individuals leasing short term or under a purchase agreement. Customers will provide a copy of driver's license and Social Security number in addition to other information requested on the application form. Commercial customers will provide federal ID number and contact name.
(b) Rental and lease customers will pay a $300.00 water security deposit.
(c) Property owners will pay a $75.00 water security deposit. (Must provide proof of ownership.)
(d) Commercial property owners will pay $250.00 water security deposit.
(e) Security deposits must be made in full before service will be turned on.
(f) Garbage cart deposit (required only if customer does not have a water account) is $25.00.
(Ord. No. 2017-001, 11-14-2017; Ord. No. 2019-007, 10-8-2019; Ord. of 12-29-20)
558:
(a) Water for temporary use will be supplied through standard services, where possible, and charged at the established metered rate.
(b) Property owners may request temporary service for a period not to exceed 48 hours without paying a security deposit but will be responsible for payment of the consumption charges at the established metered rate.
(Ord. No. 2017-001, 11-14-2017; Ord. No. 2019-007, 10-8-2019)
559:
Customers with a history of two or more late payments, disconnections, NSF checks, and/or delinquent notices in a six-month period of time may be required to post an additional security deposit so the amount of deposit held by the city is sufficient to cover the utility bills incurred by the customer in an average month peak period of time. The additional deposit required may be added to the bill for collection. If service has been disconnected, the additional deposit must be paid to the city prior to the restoration of service. Credit will be given for the amount of security deposit previously collected by the city.
(Ord. No. 2017-001, 11-14-2017; Ord. No. 2019-007, 10-8-2019)
560:
Refunds of security deposits made for utility service may be made upon the termination of such utility service, provided all indebtedness to the city for such utility service at all locations where service is provided to the same person, firm, or corporation has been paid and that the correcting and/or repairing of any damage to the city facilities and equipment has been completed. The security deposit may be applied as partial or total settlement of account balances when services are terminated, whether voluntarily or due to nonpayment of bills. At the customer's request, and if acceptable to the city, security deposits may be transferred from one customer service location to another service location used by the same customer.
(Ord. No. 2017-001, 11-14-2017; Ord. No. 2019-007, 10-8-2019)
561:
(a) The customer shall not be entitled to any interest on any funds held by the city for any purpose whatsoever, including over charges.
(b) If security deposit refund is less than $5.00 we will not refund unless specifically requested.
(Ord. No. 2017-001, 11-14-2017; Ord. No. 2019-007, 10-8-2019)
562:
The unauthorized or illegal use of water shall be billed at 150 percent of the current rate for estimated water consumption. The above charges do not preclude the city from levying other charges, including, but not limited to, a penalty not to excess $500.00 per violation per day, or taking legal action as deemed appropriate, including injunctive relief.
(Ord. No. 2017-001, 11-14-2017; Ord. No. 2019-007, 10-8-2019)
563:
(a) Damage to any city property shall be charged to the property owner or other individual as may be appropriate at the full cost of repair, including overhead, in addition to a penalty not to exceed $1,000.00 per occurrence per day as determined by the billing clerk or designated agent.
(b) If equipment has been damaged or tampered with, including, but not limited to, taking water without authorization or without having a hydrant meter installed, the party responsible for the damage, tampering, or withdrawal may be charged for the damages caused and for the estimated water and garbage services utilized, and shall also pay a penalty or surcharge as determined by the billing clerk or designated agent but not to exceed $500.00 per occurrence per day. Each such action and incident of damage, tampering, or withdrawal shall constitute a separate offense.
(c) The above charges do not preclude the city from levying other charges or taking other legal action as deemed appropriate, including injunctive relief.
(Ord. No. 2017-001, 11-14-2017; Ord. No. 2019-007, 10-8-2019)
564:
(a) In the event a water meter is not readily accessible to the appropriate city official, water consumption shall be estimated or service discontinued.
(b) A $25.00 fee may be charged for a meter test requested by a property owner who is served by a meter smaller than two inches if the meter is registering consumption accurately and/or more than one meter test was requested for the property served within the previous 24-month period. The fee charged the customer/property owner for testing meters two inches and greater shall be at the city's cost whenever requested by the property owner or agent of the property owner.
(Ord. No. 2017-001, 11-14-2017; Ord. No. 2019-007, 10-8-2019)
565:
When, upon examination, meters fail to register or the accuracy does not meet the requirements of the city water department, the account will be examined for a period of one year preceding the removal. Should there be a marked difference in consumption as shown by a defective meter and one in good repair, an additional charge or credit for under or over registration of the meter for one year shall be made.
(Ord. No. 2017-001, 11-14-2017; Ord. No. 2019-007, 10-8-2019)
566:
A refund or abatement on a bill for metered water can be made only for one of the following reasons:
(1) Where an error has been made in the reading of the meter or the preparation of the bill.
(2) When the meter, upon test, shows an average over registration greater than two percent.
(3) When any charge of the city has been paid twice or incorrectly. The original receipted bill must accompany the request for a refund. In general, all overpayments will be credited to the account and shown as a credit against the account on the next bill.
(Ord. No. 2017-001, 11-14-2017; Ord. No. 2019-007, 10-8-2019)
567:
Customers who believe a bill is in error should bring the matter to the attention of the city water department billing office for resolution before the due date of the bill. Customers who fail to timely present their objection waive their right to protest such charges.
(Ord. No. 2017-001, 11-14-2017; Ord. No. 2019-007, 10-8-2019)
568:
If a customer believes they are eligible for a hardship consideration, they may request a reduction in payment to be decided by mayor and/or city council.
(Ord. No. 2017-001, 11-14-2017; Ord. No. 2019-007, 10-8-2019)
569:
The judge of the municipal court of the city shall have the power and authority to impose fines, costs, and forfeitures for the violation of the ordinance codified in this article in an amount not to exceed $500.00 per violation per day, to imprison offenders for not more than six months per violation per day, or sentence offenders to community service for not more than 30 days per violation per day; and the municipal judge shall have the power and authority to impose any one or more, or in any combination, the punishments set forth herein when he (or she) find the facts of the case so to justify.
(Ord. No. 2017-001, 11-14-2017; Ord. No. 2019-007, 10-8-2019)
